questions.q: What does **2FA** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Two-Factor Authentication
Requiring two independent pieces of evidence to log in (e.g. password plus a code)

questions.q: What does **AES** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Advanced Encryption Standard
The standard symmetric-key algorithm for encrypting data

questions.q: What does **AI** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Artificial Intelligence
Software that performs tasks normally needing human intelligence

questions.q: What does **API** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Application Programming Interface
A defined contract that lets one piece of software request services from another

questions.q: What does **APP** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Australian Privacy Principles
The 13 principles governing how organisations handle personal information under Australian law

questions.q: What does **BPA** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Business Process Automation
Automating whole multi-step business workflows, not just single tasks

questions.q: What does **BSD** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Berkeley Software Distribution (licence)
A permissive open-source software licence

questions.q: What does **CDN** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Content Delivery Network
Geographically distributed servers that cache and serve content close to the user

questions.q: What does **CI/CD** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Continuous Integration / Continuous Deployment (Delivery)
Automating the build-test-deploy pipeline so changes ship frequently and safely

questions.q: What does **CMS** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Content Management System
Software for creating and managing website content without hand-coding each page

questions.q: What does **COMPAS** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Correctional Offender Management Profiling for Alternative Sanctions
A risk-assessment algorithm used in US courts (case study in algorithmic bias)

questions.q: What does **CORS** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing
Browser rules controlling when a page may request resources from another origin

questions.q: What does **CPU** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Central Processing Unit
The processor that executes program instructions

questions.q: What does **CR** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Code Review
Manual inspection of source code by other developers to catch defects

questions.q: What does **CSRF** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Cross-Site Request Forgery
An attack that tricks a logged-in user's browser into sending an unwanted request

questions.q: What does **CSS** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Cascading Style Sheets
The language that styles and lays out HTML content

questions.q: What does **CSV** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Comma-Separated Values
A plain-text file format storing tabular data as comma-delimited rows

questions.q: What does **CVE** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures
A public catalogue giving each known security flaw a unique identifier

questions.q: What does **CVSS** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Common Vulnerability Scoring System
A standard 0-10 score rating the severity of a security vulnerability

questions.q: What does **DARPA** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency
The US defence R&D agency (ran the autonomous-vehicle Grand Challenge)

questions.q: What does **DAST** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Dynamic Application Security Testing
Testing a running application from the outside for security flaws ("doing")

questions.q: What does **DB** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Database
An organised, queryable store of persistent data

questions.q: What does **DDoS** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Distributed Denial of Service
Overwhelming a service with traffic from many machines so it becomes unavailable

questions.q: What does **DevOps** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Development and Operations
A culture/practice uniting development and operations to automate delivery

questions.q: What does **DFD** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Data Flow Diagram
A model showing how data moves between processes, stores and external entities

questions.q: What does **DNS** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Domain Name System
The system that translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses

questions.q: What does **DOF** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Degrees Of Freedom
The number of independent movements a mechatronic system (e.g. a robot arm) can make

questions.q: What does **FK** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Foreign Key
A column that references the primary key of another table to link records

questions.q: What does **FTP** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: File Transfer Protocol
A protocol for transferring files between hosts (insecure unless secured)

questions.q: What does **GB** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Gigabyte
A unit of data storage (about one billion bytes)

questions.q: What does **GDPR** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: General Data Protection Regulation
The European Union's data-protection and privacy law

questions.q: What does **GPA** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Grade Point Average
A numeric summary of academic grades (used as example data)

questions.q: What does **GPL** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: GNU General Public License
A copyleft open-source licence requiring derivative works to stay open

questions.q: What does **HMAC** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Hash-based Message Authentication Code
A keyed hash proving a message's integrity and authenticity

questions.q: What does **HTML** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: HyperText Markup Language
The language that structures the content of web pages

questions.q: What does **HTTP** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: HyperText Transfer Protocol
The request/response protocol used to transfer web resources

questions.q: What does **HTTPS** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure
HTTP encrypted with TLS for confidentiality and integrity in transit

questions.q: What does **IDE** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Integrated Development Environment
An editor bundling coding, building, running and debugging tools in one program

questions.q: What does **IoT** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Internet of Things
Everyday physical devices (cameras, sensors) connected to the internet

questions.q: What does **IP** stand for? (it has 2 meanings in this course)
keyPoints: Intellectual Property — Creations of the mind (code, designs, content) protected by copyright, patents and trademarks
Internet Protocol — The protocol that addresses and routes data packets across networks

questions.q: What does **JPL** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Jet Propulsion Laboratory
NASA's centre for robotic space missions (Mars Climate Orbiter case study)

questions.q: What does **JS** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: JavaScript
The programming language that runs in web browsers

questions.q: What does **JSON** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: JavaScript Object Notation
A lightweight, human-readable text format for exchanging structured data

questions.q: What does **JWT** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: JSON Web Token
A compact, signed token used to carry authentication/authorisation claims

questions.q: What does **MCAS** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Maneuvering Characteristics Augmentation System
The flight-control software implicated in the Boeing 737 MAX crashes

questions.q: What does **MFA** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Multi-Factor Authentication
Requiring two or more independent factors to verify identity

questions.q: What does **MGF1** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Mask Generation Function 1
The mask-generation function used inside RSA OAEP/PSS padding

questions.q: What does **MIT** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
In licensing, the MIT License — a short, permissive open-source licence; also the US university it is named after

questions.q: What does **ML** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Machine Learning
AI systems that learn patterns from data rather than being explicitly programmed

questions.q: What does **MTTD** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Mean Time To Detect
The average time taken to notice a security incident

questions.q: What does **MTTR** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Mean Time To Respond (Recover)
The average time taken to respond to and recover from an incident

questions.q: What does **NASA** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: National Aeronautics and Space Administration
The US space agency (referenced in several engineering-failure case studies)

questions.q: What does **NESA** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: NSW Education Standards Authority
The body that sets the HSC syllabus and exams in New South Wales

questions.q: What does **NFR** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Non-Functional Requirement
A quality constraint (performance, security, usability) rather than a feature

questions.q: What does **NIST** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: National Institute of Standards and Technology
The US agency that publishes widely used security standards and frameworks

questions.q: What does **OAEP** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Optimal Asymmetric Encryption Padding
The secure padding scheme used with RSA encryption

questions.q: What does **OOP** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Object-Oriented Programming
A paradigm structuring software around objects that bundle data and behaviour

questions.q: What does **ORM** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Object-Relational Mapping
A layer that maps database tables to program objects so you write code, not raw SQL

questions.q: What does **OSS** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Open-Source Software
Software whose source code is publicly available and licensed for reuse

questions.q: What does **PCI** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Payment Card Industry (Data Security Standard)
The security standard for organisations that handle payment-card data

questions.q: What does **PEN** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Penetration test
An authorised simulated attack that chains real exploits to prove impact

questions.q: What does **PIA** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Privacy Impact Assessment
A structured review of how a project affects personal privacy

questions.q: What does **PID** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Proportional-Integral-Derivative (controller)
A closed-loop control algorithm that corrects error smoothly toward a setpoint

questions.q: What does **PK** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Primary Key
The column that uniquely identifies each row in a database table

questions.q: What does **PSS** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Probabilistic Signature Scheme
The secure padding scheme used with RSA digital signatures

questions.q: What does **PWA** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Progressive Web App
A website that can install, work offline and behave like a native app

questions.q: What does **QA** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Quality Assurance
The processes that build quality into a product, not just test for defects

questions.q: What does **RBAC** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Role-Based Access Control
Granting permissions to roles, then assigning users to those roles

questions.q: What does **ROI** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Return on Investment
The financial gain from an investment relative to its cost

questions.q: What does **RPA** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Robotic Process Automation
Software 'bots' that automate repetitive, rule-based user tasks

questions.q: What does **RSA** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Rivest-Shamir-Adleman
A widely used asymmetric (public-key) encryption and signature algorithm

questions.q: What does **SAST** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Static Application Security Testing
Analysing source code for security flaws without running it ("source")

questions.q: What does **SDLC** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Software Development Life Cycle
The staged process (requirements → design → build → test → maintain) for building software

questions.q: What does **SFTP** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: SSH File Transfer Protocol
A secure, encrypted protocol for transferring files over SSH

questions.q: What does **SHA-256** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Secure Hash Algorithm, 256-bit
A cryptographic hash producing a fixed 256-bit fingerprint of data

questions.q: What does **SMB** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Server Message Block
A network file-sharing protocol (exploited by WannaCry)

questions.q: What does **SPA** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Single-Page Application
A web app that loads one page and updates content dynamically via JavaScript

questions.q: What does **SQL** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Structured Query Language
The standard language for querying and manipulating relational databases

questions.q: What does **SQLi** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: SQL injection
An attack that injects malicious SQL through unvalidated input

questions.q: What does **SSH** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Secure Shell
An encrypted protocol for remote login and command execution

questions.q: What does **SSL** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Secure Sockets Layer
The predecessor to TLS for encrypting network connections

questions.q: What does **TCP** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Transmission Control Protocol
The protocol providing reliable, ordered delivery of data over IP

questions.q: What does **TLS** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Transport Layer Security
The protocol that encrypts and authenticates data in transit (secures HTTPS)

questions.q: What does **TOCTOU** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Time-Of-Check to Time-Of-Use
A race-condition flaw where state changes between validating and using it

questions.q: What does **UAT** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: User Acceptance Testing
Final testing by end users to confirm the software meets their needs

questions.q: What does **UI** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: User Interface
The parts of a system a user directly interacts with

questions.q: What does **URL** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Uniform Resource Locator
The address that identifies and locates a resource on the web

questions.q: What does **USD** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: United States Dollars
The currency unit used in cost/impact figures

questions.q: What does **UTC** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Coordinated Universal Time
The primary global time standard, used for unambiguous timestamps

questions.q: What does **UX** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: User Experience
The overall quality of a user's interaction with a product

questions.q: What does **VA** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Vulnerability Assessment
Systematically scanning and cataloguing known weaknesses (breadth over depth)

questions.q: What does **VPN** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Virtual Private Network
An encrypted tunnel that extends a private network across a public one

questions.q: What does **W3C** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: World Wide Web Consortium
The body that develops open web standards (HTML, CSS, WCAG)

questions.q: What does **WAF** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Web Application Firewall
A filter that inspects HTTP traffic to block web attacks

questions.q: What does **WAI** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Web Accessibility Initiative
The W3C effort that produces web accessibility guidelines

questions.q: What does **WCAG** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines
The W3C standard defining how to make web content accessible (see POUR)

questions.q: What does **XSS** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Cross-Site Scripting
An attack injecting malicious scripts into pages viewed by other users

questions.q: What does **Y2K** stand for, and what is it?
keyPoints: Year 2000 (bug)
The bug from storing years as two digits, feared to break systems in 2000
